RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generative Adversarial Network) combines parametric and non-parametric memory in the following way:

RAG models use both parametric and non-parametric memory in their architecture. The parametric memory is used to learn latent retrieval, which is a way of representing the content of the retrieved item in a way that can be used to generate new text. This latent retrieval is learned from scratch for specific tasks, such as memory networks.

The non-parametric memory, on the other hand, is used to aggregate content from multiple pieces of retrieved content. This non-parametric memory is not learned from scratch, but rather is a learned representation of the aggregated content.

In other words, RAG models use parametric memory to learn the underlying structure of the retrieved item, and non-parametric memory to aggregate content from multiple sources and represent it in a way that can be used to generate new text.
